question: At the start of round 5, your first attempt to render the round-4 reference images (default, alt-view, caustic-closeup) produced no files. Why?
answer:
Because I passed a bad --mesh path, so the program aborted during mesh loading before it ever traced or wrote anything.

What happened: in that first reference-render call I typed the mesh as /Users/peihongguo/Code/rasterizer-bunny/assets/stanford-bunny.obj, dropping the "aos/reports/" part of the real path (/Users/peihongguo/Code/aos/reports/rasterizer-bunny/assets/stanford-bunny.obj). The binary could not open the OBJ, reported the error once per scene, exited with status 1, and the trailing `ls -la out/r4_*` reported "No such file or directory".

How I know: the tool result for that call (history #24) shows stdout "mesh error: cannot open mesh: /Users/peihongguo/Code/rasterizer-bunny/assets/stanford-bunny.obj" three times — once per scene in the loop — plus stderr "ls: out/r4_*: No such file or directory" and exit_code 1. Nothing was on disk because the failure is in setup, before any dispatch or image write. After fixing the path (#26) the same three renders succeeded (#27) and produced out/r4_default.pfm (md5 53600ca347f0b76ab1a0ff894f6a8f4e), out/r4_alt-view.pfm (1f0de145...) and out/r4_caustic-closeup.pfm (0e38e718...), which are the byte-identity references used for every round-5 candidate. This was a distinct issue from the later ab_r4 problem, where a `cp -R` nesting bug left include/include and made the frozen base silently fail shader compilation.

question: At the start of round 5, your first attempt to render the round-4 reference images (default, alt-view, caustic-closeup) produced no files. Why?
answer: Because the program never got as far as rendering: in that first attempt I passed --mesh with a mistyped path — /Users/peihongguo/Code/rasterizer-bunny/assets/stanford-bunny.obj, missing the "aos/reports/" segment (the real file is /Users/peihongguo/Code/aos/reports/rasterizer-bunny/assets/stanford-bunny.obj). The mesh loader failed for all three scenes and each run printed "mesh error: cannot open mesh: /Users/peihongguo/Code/rasterizer-bunny/assets/stanford-bunny.obj" and exited with status 1 before any image was allocated, so `ls -la out/r4_*` reported "No such file or directory" (tool result #24; the shell exit code 1 came from that ls, not from a silent renderer failure). I know this directly from that tool output, which named the bad path three times, and I confirmed the diagnosis by re-running the same loop with the corrected path variable (M=/Users/peihongguo/Code/aos/reports/rasterizer-bunny/assets/stanford-bunny.obj): all three renders then succeeded at samples=16777216 and produced out/r4_default.pfm (md5 53600ca347f0b76ab1a0ff894f6a8f4e, matching the round-4 log), out/r4_alt-view.pfm (1f0de145...) and out/r4_caustic-closeup.pfm (0e38e718...) (tool results #26-#27). Note this is a different failure from the one I hit later with the frozen A/B base binary in ab_r4 (messages #70-#76), which printed nothing at all because a `cp -R` nesting bug had put the headers at ab_r4/include/include and the shader compile silently failed — that one was a real silent failure, whereas the missing reference images were simply an explicit mesh-path error I had passed on the command line.

question: At the start of round 5, your first attempt to render the round-4 reference images (default, alt-view, caustic-closeup) produced no files. Why?
answer:
The reference renders produced no files because the command passed a wrong --mesh path: I typed /Users/peihongguo/Code/rasterizer-bunny/assets/stanford-bunny.obj, dropping the "aos/reports/" part of the real path /Users/peihongguo/Code/aos/reports/rasterizer-bunny/assets/stanford-bunny.obj.

How I know: history entry #24 for that exact command shows the program's own failure message three times — once per scene — "mesh error: cannot open mesh: /Users/peihongguo/Code/rasterizer-bunny/assets/stanford-bunny.obj", plus "ls: out/r4_*: No such file or directory" and exit code 1. The program loads the OBJ before allocating or tracing anything, so it aborted at mesh loading and never wrote a PFM or PPM; nothing was wrong with the renderer or the scene configs.

Confirming evidence: re-running the same loop with the corrected path (#26-#27) immediately produced all three images with the expected output line "setup_ms=... samples=16777216 width=512 height=512 spp=64 threads_used=8 triangles=69451 bvh_nodes=81521" and the reference MD5s now used for byte-identity checks (out/r4_default.pfm 53600ca347f0b76ab1a0ff894f6a8f4e, alt-view 1f0de145..., caustic-closeup 0e38e718...).

(For disambiguation: a second, later failure in round 5 — the ab_r4 A/B base binary printing nothing — had a different cause: `cp -R` nesting created ab_r4/include/include, so the shaders directory was missing next to the base binary and newLibraryWithSource failed silently. That affected the A/B base, not these reference renders.)
